To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Echo State Networks can be used for modeling the slugging flow in gas-lift vertical risers; 2) A multiple timescale ESN is able to estimate the downhole pressure of an offshore oil well with a higher performance than a single timescale ESN; and 3) The proposed ESNs are able to estimate downhole pressure from topside platform measurements with an error that is lower than the uncertainty of the pressure sensor.

(i) a single ESN trained to simulate a gas-lift vertical riser is capable of modeling the slugging flow and the steady state; (ii) the ESN trained to predict the downhole pressure from real-world data performs better than the standard network; and (iii) the multiple timescale hierarchical ESN performs better than the regular ESN in predicting the downhole pressure.
ESNs can be trained to accurately estimate downhole pressure in gas-lifted wells, and the performance can be further improved by a hierarchical architecture.
